# tab.am — customer account API contract

**Audience:** the Laravel (Sanctum) developer replacing the mock API.

**Generated by** `node scripts/_gen_account_doc.mjs` against the running mock server at `http://localhost:3000`, so every sample below is a real response. Regenerate after any contract change.

The frontend never talks to an endpoint directly: every call is a typed method in
[`services/api.ts`](../services/api.ts) (auth methods start at `getMe`). Pointing that
file at Laravel is the whole swap — no UI change is required, which is why the
session is a plain cookie and not a bearer token.

## 1. Base rules

| Rule | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Prefix | `/api/v1` (same origin as the storefront — no CORS in the happy path) |
| Envelope | `{ data, meta?, error?: { code, message, fields? } }` |
| Success flag | `success: true` is mirrored from the pre-existing catalogue endpoints; keep it so the shared response reader stays unchanged |
| Auth | cookie `tab_market_session`, resolved server-side; `401 unauthenticated` otherwise |
| `/me/*` cache | `Cache-Control: no-store` on every `/me/*` response |
| Mutations | `POST`/`PATCH`/`DELETE` require a same-origin `Origin`; otherwise `403 same_origin_required` |
| Content type | JSON only; a non-JSON request body is `415` |
| Dates | ISO-8601 UTC strings |
| Money | integer AMD, no decimals, never a formatted string |
| Ordering | `/me/orders` newest first; `/me/addresses` default first |

## 2. Session cookie, Sanctum mapping, CSRF

The mock mints an opaque random id (`hex`, 32–128 chars) and stores the mapping
server-side. Nothing about the session is readable by JavaScript.

```text
Set-Cookie: tab_market_session=<opaque-id>; Path=/; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Max-Age=2592000; Expires=<date>; Secure
```

| Attribute | Value | Laravel equivalent |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Name | `tab_market_session` | any; the frontend is name-agnostic (it never reads the cookie) |
| HttpOnly | always | `SESSION_HTTP_ONLY=true` (default) |
| SameSite | `Lax` | `SESSION_SAME_SITE=lax` |
| Secure | always in production, and whenever the request arrived over HTTPS | `SESSION_SECURE_COOKIE=true` behind TLS |
| Path | `/` | `SESSION_PATH=/` |
| Lifetime | 30 days, **sliding**: every authenticated request refreshes it | `SESSION_LIFETIME=43200` with `expire_on_close` false, or a Sanctum personal-access-client expiry |

Sanctum specifics:

- Use the **cookie guard** (`auth:sanctum` with `Sanctum::guard()` / `web`-style stateful
  requests), not bearer tokens: `SANCTUM_STATEFUL_DOMAINS` must list `tab.am`, `www.tab.am`
  and `localhost:3000` for the dev swap, and `SESSION_DOMAIN` must match.
- Every `fetch` in `services/api.ts` sends `credentials: "same-origin"`, so cookies flow
  without extra work. Keep `XSRF-TOKEN` out of the picture or make it optional: the
  frontend does **not** read that cookie today, it relies on `SameSite=Lax` plus the
  `Origin` check that the mock already enforces. If Laravel insists on the `X-XSRF-TOKEN
  ` header, that is one extra line in `services/api.ts` — call it out before shipping.
- Expiring/invalid cookie must answer `401` with code `unauthenticated` — the client uses
  that exact code to decide "the session is gone, fall back to the guest snapshot".

## 3. Validation rules (identical on both sides)

The browser forms and the mock server import the same module,
[`lib/auth/schema.ts`](../lib/auth/schema.ts), so client and server cannot drift.
Port these rules to Laravel validators and return the same field keys.

| Field | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| `fullName` | required, sanitized, 2–100 chars |
| `phone` | required, canonicalized to E.164 `+374XXXXXXXX`; **only the length rule is enforced** (no operator allowlist — landlines and the dev test number must pass) |
| `password` (register) | required, 8–72 chars |
| `password` (login) | presence + ≤72 chars only — applying registration rules at login would leak how an account was created |
| `acceptTerms` | required `true` |
| `email` | optional, ≤120 chars, basic `a@b.c` shape |
| `label` | optional, ≤24 |
| `region`, `city` | required, ≤40 |
| `street` | required, ≤80 |
| `building` | required, ≤20 |
| `entrance` | optional, ≤20 · `floor` ≤8 · `apartment` ≤10 · `intercom` ≤24 |
| `recipientName` | optional, ≤100 |
| `comment` | optional, ≤240 |
| `isDefault` | boolean; exactly one default per user — setting one demotes the rest in the same write |
| addresses per user | 20 max → `409 address_limit_reached` |

Input handling that the mock does and a Laravel form request must keep doing:
control characters and repeated spaces are stripped, every string is trimmed, and
**unknown keys are ignored rather than rejected**. Phone canonicalization accepts
`095…`, `+374 95…`, `(95) 53-04-35`, `00 374 …` and any spacing; the trunk `0` is
dropped only when nine digits remain, so an eight-digit number with a leading zero
survives the round trip.

## 4. Error codes

| `error.code` | HTTP | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `unauthenticated` | 401 | no or expired session |
| `invalid_credentials` | 401 | wrong phone **or** wrong password — the two are indistinguishable on purpose |
| `validation_failed` | 422 | `error.fields` maps field key → localized message |
| `account_exists` | 409 | phone already registered; deliberately neutral |
| `address_limit_reached` | 409 | 20 addresses |
| `not_found` | 404 | unknown order id |
| `method_not_allowed` | 405 | — |
| `same_origin_required` | 403 | cross-origin mutation |
| `invalid_payload` | 400 | body is not a JSON object |
| `rate_limited` | 429 | throttle tripped; `Retry-After` seconds are set |
| `feature_disabled` | 404 | dev-only endpoint reached in production |
| `otp_not_implemented` | 501 | contract-only endpoint |
| `password_reset_not_implemented` | 501 | contract-only endpoint |

`message` is always customer-facing Armenian and owned by the backend — the UI prints
it verbatim, so the Laravel app must localize at the API, not at the Blade layer.

## 5. Rate limiting

Fixed window, keyed per **IP + normalized phone**: 5 attempts, then a 10-minute lockout
with a friendly message and `Retry-After`. Successful credentials reset the bucket.
In Laravel, a named rate limiter keyed on the IP plus the normalized phone
reproduces it. The storefront shows the server message and
disables nothing, so a wrong `Retry-After` is only a cosmetic problem.

## 6. Endpoints

| Method | Path | Auth | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| POST | `/auth/register` | — | create account + start session (auto-login) |
| POST | `/auth/login` | — | start session |
| POST | `/auth/logout` | any | destroy session |
| GET | `/me` | required | profile snapshot |
| PATCH | `/me` | required | `fullName`, `email` only — phone is read-only here |
| GET | `/me/addresses` | required | list, default first |
| POST | `/me/addresses` | required | create |
| PATCH | `/me/addresses/{id}` | required | update / set default |
| DELETE | `/me/addresses/{id}` | required | delete; returns the remaining list |
| GET | `/me/orders` | required | order summaries, newest first |
| POST | `/me/orders` | required | attach an order the storefront just placed |
| GET | `/me/orders/{id}` | required | one order (id, not the printed number) |
| GET | `/auth/dev-demo` | **dev only** | hands the quick-login chip its credentials |
| POST | `/auth/otp/request` | — | contract only, `501` |
| POST | `/auth/otp/verify` | — | contract only, `501` |
| POST | `/auth/password/reset` | — | contract only, `501` |

### 6.1 No PII in browser storage

Whatever Laravel returns, the frontend keeps this invariant: the session id lives only
in the HttpOnly cookie; the phone number lives only in the request/response and in
component state; nothing about auth is written to `localStorage`/`sessionStorage`
(verified: `localStorage` holds only `tab-cart-storage`, `sessionStorage` is empty,
`document.cookie` is `""` while `/api/v1/me` answers `200`).

The document-level snapshot is the one place user data crosses to the client, and it is
**minimal**: `{ id, fullName, maskedPhone }` — masked, never the real number.

## 8. The document cache rule (easy to break, hard to notice)

The session snapshot is inlined into the HTML document by the server
(`<!--TABA_SESSION-->` in [`index.html`](../index.html)), which is what stops the header
from flickering "log in" for a returning customer. That only works if the document is
**never stored**: a cached shell revalidated with `ETag`/`If-None-Match` comes back as a
`304` with no body, so there is nothing to rewrite, and the customer sees the logged-out
UI next to a perfectly valid cookie.

Every HTML response therefore needs:

```text
Cache-Control: no-store
Vary: Cookie
```

and must not carry `ETag` or `Last-Modified`. In Laravel this is one response middleware
on the route that serves the SPA entry point (or `no-store` on the SSR responses if the
app is server-rendered later).

## 9. Deliberately not built

| Feature | Why | What the contract already reserves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SMS OTP login / phone change | needs the shop's SMS provider; phone change is a security-sensitive verified flow | `POST /auth/otp/request`, `POST /auth/otp/verify` (`501 otp_not_implemented`) |
| Password reset | same SMS dependency | `POST /auth/password/reset` (`501`); the UI shows a "not available yet" panel, never a fake form |
| Attaching earlier **guest** orders to a new account | only possible by verifying the phone via OTP | — |
| Account deletion / data export | legal review needed | — |
| A real order ledger | the storefront generates the number client-side for guests today; see §10 | `POST /api/v1/orders` already exists as a Next-style route that is not served in this Vite build |

## 10. Known gaps the backend team should know about

- **Guest orders are simulated.** `services/api.ts#submitOrder` exists and posts to
  `/api/v1/orders`, but the checkout flow does not call it: the number comes from
  `generateOrderId()` and tracking falls back to client fixtures. A real checkout
  integration is a separate piece of work — the account feature deliberately did not
  touch the guest path.
- **Checkout validation still uses `alert()`** ([`app/checkout/page.tsx`](../app/checkout/page.tsx)).
  Pre-existing, out of scope, but it blocks the tab and is inconsistent with the inline
  `aria-live` errors used everywhere else.
- **`components/checkout/OrderSuccess.tsx` prints an unresolved placeholder** ("stock code ()")
  on the confirmation screen. Pre-existing copy bug, unrelated to accounts.
- **Privacy / Terms pages do not exist** in this codebase, so the register consent checkbox
  links to nothing new: it references the targets the footer already uses. If those routes
  stay absent, the checkbox copy must be reworded before launch — it currently asserts
  consent to documents the customer cannot read.
- **`/account` protection is client-side** (a guard in `src/App.tsx` redirects to
  `/?auth=login&next=…`). With a server-rendered Laravel, keep `next` validation
  server-side too: the mock requires a same-origin relative path (leading `/`, no `//`,
  re-parsed with `new URL()`), which is what makes `?next=https://evil.com` a no-op.

## 11. What the storefront calls, in order

1. document request → server inlines `{ id, fullName, maskedPhone }`
2. `store/useAuth.ts` adopts that snapshot (no persist, nothing written to storage)
3. login / register → `POST /auth/*` → `router.refresh()` equivalent → header updates
4. `/account/orders` → `GET /me/orders`; `/account/profile` → `GET|PATCH /me`;
   `/account/addresses` → `GET|POST|PATCH|DELETE /me/addresses`
5. `/checkout` while authenticated → `GET /me` + `GET /me/addresses` once, into
   component state only (prefill); after the order is placed → `POST /me/orders`
   and optionally `POST /me/addresses` when the customer ticked "save this address".

A Laravel implementation that satisfies sections 1–7 will run the existing UI
unchanged.
